discussion_comments.comment_body:
Fixed in 1653c81b.

The force dialog now keeps the warning, status row, and buttons on separate rows. At inner heights of eight or more it uses the two-line warning. At seven rows it uses a compact single-line warning with status on the next row. Below seven rows it replaces the branch note with the compact warning so status and buttons still fit.

The client test now renders the confirmation at 60x11 as well as 60x20 and asserts the compact warning and the delete button both remain visible.

Fixed. Native macOS testing confirmed that two 600-byte lines are delivered intact with normal PTY backpressure. The preflight now scans the entire encoded text plus submission keys before any write, using the current termios delimiters, CR transformations, quoting and control precedence. It checks each canonical line instead of aggregate submission length.

Real PTY tests cover LF/CR/custom EOL/EOF multiline delivery and a valid first line followed by an oversized second line, which is rejected without writing either line. Additional cases cover quoted/translated delimiters, control-character precedence and PARMRK.

Reviewed against 6cba6c647b8d4774a5d52a57e8dcb2e1b9d11e4c.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Confirmed. I reproduced this with the existing keyboard-copy test under copy_on_select=false. I am changing the copy request to take its live-range policy explicitly from the caller, so keyboard copy mode keeps its revision check even after exit_copy_mode takes the state. The correction and regression check are being validated before pushing.

Fixed in 7e0df8c3. The caller now explicitly selects live-range copying only for manual Ctrl+C; keyboard copy mode and automatic copying retain content_revision. The existing keyboard-copy test now runs with copy_on_select=false and asserts the revision remains present. It failed before this correction; just check now passes all 2816 Rust tests and repository checks.

Fixed in 8ff47a8. The text now renders into `input_rect.width - 1` while the full field is still cleared, so the clamped caret always lands on a blank cell.

Confirmed the failure first: with the text drawn into the full width, a 200-character name put `"a"` under the caret. The overflow test now asserts the clamped cell is `" "` and the cell to its left is `"a"`, and it fails without the change.

`just lint` is clean and `cargo nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast -E 'all()'` gives 3,188 run / 3,185 passed / 3 failed — the same three that fail on a clean master checkout on this machine (`pane_spawn_cwd_fallback_in_server`, `live_handoff_keeps_unmanaged_agent_name_bound_to_saved_session`, `multi_client_client_crash_sigkill_does_not_affect_server`); CI's ubuntu `check` covers them.
Fixed in 51de0851: the test now verifies that the path is actually untraversable and explicitly skips the assertion for privileged processes that can still traverse mode `000` directories.
